BUS.G12.T3.PRESENT.A1.title: Presentation & data response
BUS.G12.T3.PRESENT.A1.description: Accurate, succinct verbal and non-verbal presentation of business information, including the criteria for a logical and effective presentation, the process and style of using visual aids, responding professionally to questions and feedback, and amending plans and documents as necessary.
BUS.G12.T3.PRESENT.A1.recovery_strategy: An effective presentation knows its audience, puts the most important information first, and uses clear visuals. After feedback, amend the plan and documents and carry the improvements into future work.

questions.question: An effective presentation should be designed around:
options: The needs and level of its audience
questions.expected: The needs and level of its audience
questions.memo: Knowing the audience lets you pitch the content and language at the right level so the message lands.

questions.question: True or false: The most important information should be presented first.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: Leading with the key information ensures the audience gets the main message, even if attention or time fades.

questions.question: Answering questions about figures and business information presented is called a _________ response.
questions.expected: data
questions.memo: A data response involves reading, interpreting and answering questions on presented business information and figures.

questions.question: Which of these is a visual aid for presenting data clearly?
questions.expected: A graph
questions.memo: A graph is a visual (non-verbal) aid that shows data and trends clearly.

questions.question: True or false: After receiving feedback, a presenter should amend the work where needed.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: Acting on feedback by amending plans and documents improves the work and future presentations.

questions.question: When responding to questions, a presenter should not _________.
questions.expected: argue
questions.memo: A professional presenter answers and clarifies calmly rather than arguing with the questioner.

questions.question: Sort each feature into effective or ineffective presentation.

items.text: Clear headings and key points first
Tiny, cluttered, unreadable slides
Simple charts that show the data
Reading dense text word-for-word
Language pitched to the audience
Ignoring all questions

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Effective: clear structure, simple charts, suitable language. Ineffective: cluttered slides, reading dense text, ignoring questions.

questions.question: Which is a criterion for a logical, effective presentation of information?
options: Know your audience and use clear headings, charts and the most important points first
Use as many long words as possible
Hide the key message at the very end
questions.expected: Know your audience and use clear headings, charts and the most important points first
questions.memo: Effective presentations are audience-aware, well-structured, and lead with the key points supported by clear visuals.

questions.question: Put the stages of delivering and improving a presentation in order.

items.text: Prepare the content and visuals for the audience
Deliver the presentation clearly
Respond professionally to questions and feedback
Amend the work based on the feedback

questions.expected: prepare, present, questions, amend
questions.memo: Prepare, present, handle questions and feedback, then amend the work — that order improves both the message and future versions.

questions.question: Knowing your _________ lets you pitch a presentation at the right level.
questions.expected: audience
questions.memo: Understanding the audience shapes the content, depth and language so the message is understood.

questions.question: How should a presenter handle critical but fair feedback?
options: Listen, thank the person, and use it to improve the work
Take it personally and refuse to continue
questions.expected: Listen, thank the person, and use it to improve the work
questions.memo: Fair feedback is valuable; a professional listens, acknowledges it and amends the work accordingly.

questions.question: True or false: Amending plans and documents after feedback can improve future presentations.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: Carrying improvements from feedback into the documents and future plans makes later work stronger.

questions.question: Sort each response to questions and feedback into professional or unprofessional.

items.text: Answering all questions calmly
Becoming aggressive when challenged
Admitting and correcting an error
Blaming the audience for not understanding
Offering to follow up on an unknown answer
Refusing to take any feedback

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Professional: answer calmly, correct errors, offer to follow up. Unprofessional: aggression, blaming the audience, refusing feedback.

questions.question: Why are charts and graphs useful in a data-response presentation?
options: They show figures, patterns and comparisons quickly and clearly
They hide the data from the audience
They always replace the need for any explanation
They make the data impossible to read
questions.expected: They show figures, patterns and comparisons quickly and clearly
questions.memo: Charts and graphs turn raw figures into clear visual patterns, helping the audience grasp the data fast.

questions.question: A presenter is asked a question they genuinely cannot answer. What is the professional response?
options: Admit it honestly and offer to find out and follow up
Make up a confident but false answer
questions.expected: Admit it honestly and offer to find out and follow up
questions.memo: Honesty plus a commitment to follow up keeps the presenter credible; bluffing risks giving wrong information.

questions.question: Clear _________ help organise information so the audience can follow it.
questions.expected: headings
questions.memo: Clear headings (and subheadings) structure the information so the audience can follow the flow.

questions.question: Put the steps of an effective data-response presentation in order.

items.text: Read and understand the data provided
Organise the key figures and points
Present them clearly with suitable visuals
Respond to questions and amend if needed

questions.expected: read, organise, present, respond
questions.memo: Understand the data, organise the key points, present them with clear visuals, then respond to questions and amend.

questions.question: After a presentation, the audience raises several valid concerns. What is the best response?
options: Note the concerns, amend the plan and documents, and apply the lessons next time
Argue that the audience misunderstood everything
questions.expected: Note the concerns, amend the plan and documents, and apply the lessons next time
questions.memo: Valid feedback should be recorded and acted on by amending the work and improving future presentations.

questions.question: Why is the ability to amend information after feedback an important business skill?
options: It keeps plans and documents accurate and shows responsiveness, building trust
It is unnecessary because first drafts are always perfect
It wastes time with no benefit
It signals weakness and should be avoided
questions.expected: It keeps plans and documents accurate and shows responsiveness, building trust
questions.memo: Updating work in response to feedback keeps it accurate and relevant and shows stakeholders the business listens and improves.

questions.question: Which presenter is most likely to communicate business data effectively?
options: One who knows the audience, leads with key points, uses clear visuals and handles questions calmly
One who reads dense text aloud and argues with questioners
One who hides the main message and uses cluttered slides
One who ignores the audience entirely
questions.expected: One who knows the audience, leads with key points, uses clear visuals and handles questions calmly
questions.memo: Effective communication combines audience awareness, a clear structure, good visuals and a calm, professional handling of questions.
